subject.title: [security] Non-admin bearer bridge sessions remain active after shared-token rotation

question: Should Crabbox treat `CRABBOX_SHARED_TOKEN` rotation as an immediate revocation event for already-open non-admin bearer WebVNC, Code viewer, and egress bridge sessions?
rationale: The source shows the stale-session gap, but enforcing immediate failure changes live bridge semantics and requires deciding what non-secret shared-token provenance should be stored in bridge/session state.

options.title: Enforce shared-token bridge revocation
options.body: Add revocable shared-token provenance to non-admin bearer bridge grants and fail closed when the current configured token or grant version no longer matches.

options.title: Document bounded live-session survival
options.body: Keep existing live shared-token bridges until disconnect or lease end and document that rotation only blocks new shared-token requests.

options.title: Fold into a broader bridge-auth design
options.body: Hold this issue for a unified policy across bearer, GitHub, admin, control, restored, and ticketed bridge authorization.

recommendation.title: Enforce shared-token bridge revocation
recommendation.body: Add revocable shared-token provenance to non-admin bearer bridge grants and fail closed when the current configured token or grant version no longer matches.
